### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via DataEngineQueryOptionsSchema (symbol, a top-level const), EngineQueryOptionsSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **147** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e6c440900072a2d2423474962db9c7db6011b845` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0c987b6e7b8af0bb4e2dc1352a1c4b151c366b2f` — the merge of head `ba84865301c609c8167b187aebdf0109f34dbd37` into base `e6c440900072a2d2423474962db9c7db6011b845`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0c987b6e7b8af0bb4e2dc1352a1c4b151c366b2f && git checkout 0c987b6e7b8af0bb4e2dc1352a1c4b151c366b2f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e6c440900072a2d2423474962db9c7db6011b845 ba84865301c609c8167b187aebdf0109f34dbd37 && git checkout -B drift-repro e6c440900072a2d2423474962db9c7db6011b845 && git merge --no-ff ba84865301c609c8167b187aebdf0109f34dbd37

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e6c440900072a2d2423474962db9c7db6011b845
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e6c440900072a2d2423474962db9c7db6011b845` → pass the list as

### ① Derived judgments

1. **One source, moved not copied, and the move is forced.** The head holds exactly one `const transportProjectionArray` and one `const TransportProjectionStringSchema` (data-engine.zod.ts :106-111); the block removed at the old site (:910-936 on main) is byte-identical to the block added at :78-111 except for the one added paragraph and "members below" rewritten to "`QueryTransportParamsSchema` members", which is true of the new position. The TDZ claim is true in the code: `lazySchema` (lazy-schema.ts) returns a Proxy whose first property access runs the factory, and `RpcQueryOptionsSchema = EngineQueryOptionsSchema.extend({...})` (:810) is a bare module-level statement, so importing the module runs `EngineQueryOptionsSchema`'s factory at load, which now calls `transportProjectionArray` (:140). Left at :910, that `const` would still be in its temporal dead zone at :810 — a `ReferenceError` at import. Under `OS_EAGER_SCHEMAS=1` every factory runs at its own line, so the position above :135 is required on that path too. All four members (:140, :218, :813, :1525) call the one helper; `fields` passes `FieldNodeSchema`, the other three `z.string()`, as `$select` and `select` do (:1067, :1088).
2. **Behaviour-neutral for #26949's members.** `QueryTransportParamsSchema` (:1050) is lazy, so the helper's position relative to it does not change what the factory builds: `$select` and `select` are the same union of the same string arm and the same `z.array(member.regex(/\S/)).min(1)` construction, same regexes, same two messages (`Name at least one field`, `A field name cannot be blank`), same `.describe()` texts built from the same `PROJECTION_ACCEPT_SET`. `GetDataRequestSchema.select` (protocol.zod.ts :2435) and `HttpFindQueryParamsSchema.select` (:2386) still read `QueryTransportParamsSchema.shape.select.unwrap().unwrap().options[1|0]` — untouched by this diff. Each `transportProjectionArray(FieldNodeSchema)` call clones `FieldNodeSchema` through `.regex()`, so `fields` and `$select` share no mutable node and `FieldNodeSchema`'s own retired-object-form `error` map (query.zod.ts :368) rides along unchanged. The reference page's `QueryTransportParams` rows (data-engine.mdx :1310, :1317) are unchanged on the head, as `check:docs` inside the green `TypeScript Type Check` job confirms.
3. **All the published transport and engine-side declarations of the read projection now agree.** `QueryTransportParamsSchema.select` / `$select`, `GetDataRequestSchema.select`, `HttpFindQueryParamsSchema.select`, `EngineQueryOptionsSchema.fields`, `RpcQueryOptionsSchema.select` (so `DataEngineFindRequestSchema.query`, `DataEngineFindOneRequestSchema.query`, two arms of `DataEngineRequestSchema`), `DataEngineQueryOptionsSchema.select` and `DataEngineVectorFindRequestSchema.fields` all refuse `[]` and a blank member with the same two messages. `QuerySchema.fields` (query.zod.ts :519, so also `expand[rel].fields`) stays `z.array(FieldNodeSchema)`: that is the authored QueryAST (views, reports), ruled outside this family in review 6455655029 ① 3 and door-refused at runtime; not a member of this card.
4. **`FieldNodeSchema` admits no object node.** It is `z.string({ error })` whose map only rewrites the `invalid_type` message for the removed `{ field, fields, alias }` form (#4196, ADR-0049); an object entry is refused before the blank-member regex is reached, with the retirement prescription, exactly as on `$select`. The blank-member rule therefore applies to strings only, which is the whole domain.
5. **Readers, measured on `origin/main` `acc9c57d0a`.** Runtime parsers of any of the four members: none. `EngineQueryOptionsSchema` is read outside spec only for its key list — runtime `action-execution.ts` :2047 (`Object.keys(...shape)`, resolved lazily) and objectql `engine-unknown-option.test.ts` :242/:253-254 (`Object.keys(schema.shape)` minus tombstones against `ENGINE_FIND_OPTION_KEYS`, engine.ts :684); spec's own `hook-api.test.ts` :204-209 pins the same key set for `HookQuery` (hook-api.ts :143, an `Omit` over `EngineQueryOptions`, so `string[]` in and out). No key is added or removed, so all three pins hold — `Test Core` 8/8 green. `RpcQueryOptionsSchema` is module-private and reached only through the three request schemas; `DataEngineRequestSchema`, `DataEngineFindRequestSchema`, `DataEngineFindOneRequestSchema`, `DataEngineVectorFindRequestSchema`, `DataEngineQueryOptionsSchema` and `DataEngineContractSchema` have no reference outside `packages/spec` except the generated reference page's import line (references/data/data-engine.mdx :25), `kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx` :102 (a TS interface listing, `fields?: FieldNode[]`, still true) and :637 (names the legacy schema deprecated, still true), and CHANGELOG prose. `DataEngineContractSchema` embeds `EngineQueryOptionsSchema` in `find` / `findOne` `z.function` inputs (:577-585) and is on `unemitted-schemas.baseline.json` :48; nothing parses it. `packages/client` imports none of these schemas; the one client hit for `select: []` (index.ts :427) is #26910's own-side fix of a GET door call. In-repo callers sending `fields: []` / `select: []` to an engine query: none — every non-test hit under `packages`, `ui`, `examples`, `apps` is a result or metadata shape (cli orphan rows, security field readers, analytics result envelopes, screen-node metadata, UI state). Nothing on this tree can newly fail to parse.
6. **Authored metadata: none of the four is one.** `git grep` over `packages/spec/src` finds the four names in no `.zod.ts` outside data-engine.zod.ts except as prose (`action-params.zod.ts` :373, `query.zod.ts` :215/:399); no metadata type, saved query, dataset, report or AI tool argument schema embeds `EngineQueryOptionsSchema`, `DataEngineQueryOptionsSchema` or the request schemas. The authored projection is `QuerySchema.fields`, untouched. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right and the ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is honest: no stored row can newly fail, nothing for a conversion layer to rewrite, no tombstone owed (no key moves). The category is one of the gate's six (`check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` :553-560); exactly one marker, in the changeset; `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` green on the head.
7. **Generated surfaces.** The JSON Schema for the four members gains `minItems: 1` and a per-item non-blank `pattern` — a `min_length` and a `string_format` check, not `custom` (`refinement-projection.ts` :50), so no `dropped-refinements` row is owed and the ledger is unchanged. `json-schema.manifest/data.json` is a name list (`data/EngineQueryOptions` :68, `data/DataEngineQueryOptions` :44, `data/DataEngineVectorFindRequest` :49, `data/DataEngineFindRequest` :41), and `api-surface`, `declaration-map`, `export-origins`, `authorable-surface` are export- or key-level: none moves. The reference page renders `.describe()` only (the `EngineQueryOptions.fields` and `DataEngineVectorFindRequest.fields` rows carry an empty Description on main, :1121 and :880) and none of the four members had or gains one, so no page regenerates; the dev's "No `.describe()` changes" is true, and the changed text on the members is TSDoc, which the generator does not read. `check:generated` 14/14 up to date is therefore the expected reading, and the `TypeScript Type Check` job that runs it is green. `gen:openapi` writes the gitignored `json-schema/openapi.json` at build (build-openapi.ts :21), ungated as AGENTS.md records. `check:doc-authoring` (in the green `Lint & Repo Gates`) does not flag the `(#26954)` TSDoc tags; the file already carries `(#8057)` the same way at :272.
8. **The ADR-0049 note (:1551-1558) is unchanged and its measurable sentences hold at the head.** "every arm below now has zero readers in this repo": true — no runtime parser outside spec's own tests (judgment 5). "there is no Virtual Data Engine implementation, only this schema describing one": true — `git grep` for a virtual data engine / Virtual ObjectQL implementation outside spec finds nothing. "an ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove candidate, deliberately left standing": true — the seat ruled align, not retire (claim 6456968829), so the candidacy stands. "it is tracked separately": see ③.
9. **Declarations.** PR body and changeset both carry line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` (the `— prose` suffix is the spelling `clause2-line.mjs` :115-121 reads the arm from) and `Metadata-protocol: none`; the PR body carries the `Skills-docs: none — REASON` line owed for a `(narrowing)` arm (pm-dispatch SKILL.md :313, #26369 B) — the value `none` is right (judgment 11), the reason's wording is not (③). The changeset's `**BREAKING**` banner names the four members, says what breaks (external parsers and generated clients sending an empty projection), carries Before / Now / Unchanged and the remedy, and does not claim a runtime refusal; the PR title carries the `!`. The `Unchanged` bullet and the PR body's Acceptance notes both state that `engine.find(object, { fields: [] })` still reads every column; the TSDoc "at least one, none blank" describes the declaration's accept set and nothing in the diff says the engine refuses it — consistent with #27008, which is open and names exactly that gap.
10. **Tests are honest and the ablation arithmetic matches the block.** Every refusal case asserts `success === false`, the issue path (`['fields']` / `['fields', 1]`, `['query', 'select', …]`, `['query', 'fields', …]`, `['select', …]`, `['fields', …]` on vectorFind) and that the message equals the transport sibling's for the same value, with `sibling()` first asserting the sibling itself refuses (so `toBe` never compares two undefineds); the first block also pins the sibling's own path. A zod 4 union that leaves one non-aborted branch surfaces that branch's issues directly, which is why `issues[0]` on `$select` / `select` is the array arm's `too_small` / `invalid_format` and not an `invalid_union` — and `Test Core` green on the head is the proof. The KEPT cases pin the fold (`select` → `fields`) and non-empty lists unchanged. Reported ablations: `fields` reverted → 12 red = 3 values × (EngineQueryOptions + 3 request schemas' `query.fields`); RPC `select` reverted → 9 = 3 × 3; legacy `select` → 3; vectorFind `fields` → 6 = 3 × 2. Each is exactly the case count that exercises the reverted arm, so the reported reds do exercise the new arms.
11. **Skills.** `git grep` over `skills/**`: no sentence teaches an empty projection; the engine `fields` examples are named lists (`objectstack-query/rules/filters.md` :105 `fields: ['id']`, `SKILL.md` :25 lists `fields` among `engine.find` options, evals :37) and `objectui/guides/data-integration.md` :82 is `$select: ['name', 'email']`. Nothing taught there becomes false; `Skills-docs: none` is the right value.
12. **Scope.** Three paths, all on the claim's file surface (data-engine.zod.ts, its test, one `@objectstack/spec` changeset); no generated artifact needed regenerating; no governed surface; 198 changed lines. The branch name `claude/project-thread-pz6ul8` is the platform-assigned thread branch, declared in the claim.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` **patch** — correct: the one published package the diff moves; `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch` and keeps the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 marker (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3), the same level #26949 took for the same kind of narrowing. No other package publishes anything from this diff. `Check Changeset` green twice on the head (01:08Z and, after the body edit, 02:01Z).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation "the #26949 block moves above `EngineQueryOptionsSchema`": forced by the non-lazy `.extend` at :810 (① 1), one copy on the head, behaviour-neutral for the earlier members (① 2). Accepted.
- Seat request folded in (`DataEngineQueryOptionsSchema.select`, `DataEngineVectorFindRequestSchema.fields`): same file, same family, same ruling, named in the claim's file surface and in the changeset's banner and marker; the round-1 out-of-scope finding is thereby closed in-PR, not left owed. Accepted.
- Dev acceptance note "the declaration is narrower than the in-process engine, by design": true on the code (engine.ts :13572 projects only when `ast.fields.length` is above zero, nothing parses the options with this schema); no sentence in the diff or body claims a runtime refusal; the seat filed #27008 (open). No action here.
- **`Skills-docs:` reason overstated — correct the PR body line, no code change.** The line reads "no file under `skills/**` teaches an engine `fields` or RPC `select` projection, empty or not"; `skills/objectstack-query/rules/filters.md` :105 (`fields: ['id']`) and `SKILL.md` :25 do teach the engine `fields` projection, named. The true reason is the one #26949's body gave: `skills/**` teaches only named projections and never an empty one, so nothing there changes. The value `none` stands; the owning seat should rewrite the reason in the body before landing. Not a FAIL reason.
- **ADR-0049 note, fourth sentence: "it is tracked separately"** — I could not locate the tracker from the repo-scoped API (the search endpoint is not available to this session), and card #26954, which carried the enforce-or-remove question, closes with this PR having ruled "align, not retire; the note stays an open candidate". The sentence predates the diff and the diff makes no claim about it, so it is not this PR's defect; escalated to the seat to NAME the tracker in the card, or FILE one (Prime Directive 10), so the candidate the note promises is tracked somewhere that outlives #26954.
- Observation, no action owed: because none of the four members carries a `.describe()`, the published reference rows for them (`EngineQueryOptions.fields` :1121, `DataEngineVectorFindRequest.fields` :880) stay silent on the accept set that `QueryTransportParams.$select` / `select` state in theirs. A `.describe()` phrased as the declaration's accept set (not "is refused at runtime") would surface the rule to generated clients and readers without contradicting #27008; a candidate for the #27008 follow-up, not this card.
- Dogfood owed by the `(narrowing)` arm: CI's `Dogfood Regression Gate (N/3)` shards are path-filtered off this PR (skipped); the dev reports the full battery on `ba848653` (344 files / 2784 tests passed, 20 skipped, lock `VERDICT command-exit 0`) and the same counts on `17ce2dfb`. No runtime path changes on this tree (① 5), so the carry rests on the diff reading; recorded as the dev's reading.

Also green and load-bearing: `Check Changeset` (twice), `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` (the ADR-0087 marker gate), `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure`, `Spec property liveness`, `PR-body guards`. ## 维护者速读 (席位终稿)

- 改了什么：数据引擎一侧还有四个投影声明允许空投影，现在与 #26949 的同一条规则对齐：`EngineQueryOptionsSchema.fields`、`RpcQueryOptionsSchema.select`、`DataEngineQueryOptionsSchema.select`、`DataEngineVectorFindRequestSchema.fields`。空数组和空白成员都会被拒，拒绝文案与兄弟声明逐字相同。规则只有一处来源，是挪过来的，不是复制。
- 为什么改：其余已发布的投影声明都拒空投影，只有这四处还放行；读这些 schema 生成客户端或写代码的 AI 会学到相反的规则。
- 风险与回滚：仓内没有任何运行时用这四份 schema 解析请求，线上请求零变化。会受影响的只有仓外直接用这些导出 schema 解析、且发了空投影的代码。进程内 `engine.find(obj, { fields: [] })` 仍读全部列，已另立卡 #27008。回滚 = revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/spec/src/data/data-engine.zod.ts` 的 `transportProjectionArray`（约 :106），以及它被挪到 `EngineQueryOptionsSchema` 之上的原因：非 lazy 的 `.extend` 在模块加载时就会执行。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/data/data-engine.test.ts`，预期全绿；投影相关 44 项，覆盖四个成员的空数组、空白成员和路径。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

席位意见：接受。契约复核 PASS（6458779713）。复核提出的两个提示已处理：PR 描述里 `Skills-docs: none` 的理由原先写错了，已改写（技能只教非空的 `fields`）；数据块注释说「另行跟踪」却没有对应的卡，已立卡 #27028。

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · `domain:spec` seat 3 · `os-support-ai` · session `session_01WGufzgbJhFoXYsLSe5WSPP` · 2026-10-28T02:16Z

Head: `ba84865301c609c8167b187aebdf0109f34dbd37` · card #26954 · claim 6456968829 (seat ruling: align, do not retire)

1. **形态:** a draft PR to `main`. Its only closing keyword is `Fixes #26954`. It touches 3 paths, +163 / −35: the declarations, their tests and one `@objectstack/spec` changeset, all inside the claim surface. `check-governed-merges --pr 27007` reports NOT governed, 198 lines, so the ordinary queue landing applies. The assignee is `os-support-ai`.
